wifiPanel.title: Hand the network "{ssid}" to the hornets
wifiPanel.intro: The network and password come from the fields above (save them first). Choose how to hand them over, and to which hornets.

stage.title: Prepare a spare network
stage.what: Nothing is switched or restarted: the hornet stays on its current network and only remembers this one as a spare. It moves to it by itself when it can no longer join its current one, that is, after you change the name or password on the router.
stage.steps: Choose the hornets below and press "Prepare a spare network"|Wait in Events for "spare network saved" from each|Change the network name or password on the router|In a minute or two the hornets move by themselves, Events show "now on ..."
stage.when: Works for changing the password of the same network too. Safe: while you have not touched the router, nothing changes.

switch.title: Switch now (a trial)
switch.what: The hornet restarts at once and tries this network. If it reaches the hive, the network becomes its main one and the old one stays as the spare. If not within a minute, it goes back to the old one by itself.
switch.steps: The new network must already work next to the old one (for example a second name on the router)|Choose ONE hornet and press "Switch"|Wait in Events: "now on ..." or "network did not work, the old one stayed"|If all is well, switch the others
switch.when: Not for changing the password of the same network: while the router knows only one password, the board cannot test the new one.

wifiPanel.choose: Which hornets (only those online and awake)
wifiPanel.asleep: asleep, the command would not reach it
wifiPanel.oldFirmware: old firmware: prepare it over USB or update it
wifiPanel.summaryStage: What will happen: {names} will remember the network "{ssid}" as a spare. Nothing is switched or restarted.
wifiPanel.summarySwitch: What will happen: {names} will restart now and try the network "{ssid}". If they do not reach the hive within a minute they go back to the old one.
wifiPanel.switchWarning: If you have already changed the network or password on the router, the old network does not work and the board has nowhere to go back to: it will have to be fixed over USB.
wifiPanel.confirmStage: Remember the network "{ssid}" as a spare on: {names}? Nothing is switched.
wifiPanel.confirmSwitch: Restart {names} and try the network "{ssid}"? If they do not reach the hive within a minute, they go back to the old one.
wifiPanel.afterStage: Next: wait for "spare network saved" from every hornet, then change the router.
wifiPanel.afterSwitch: Next: in a minute look at "Wi-Fi switch" of each hornet: "now on" or "the old one stayed".

swarm.title: Swarm
swarm.removeConfirm: Remove “{name}”? The board loses access to the hive; its history stays.
swarm.replaceHint: New board for {id}: flash it and enter this code in the wizard's setup step (or with the enroll command). The old board loses access.
swarm.sleepSaved: Saved. The hornet applies it at its next wake-up
swarm.sleepHint: For battery hornets: wakes, sends a reading and sleeps. Needs a GPIO16–RST jumper (docs/hornet-esp01-battery.md)
swarm.pinsSaved: Saved. The hornet applies it as soon as it gets the new config: right away if online, or at its next wake-up
swarm.pinsRejected: Pins not saved: a conflict or a bad number
swarm.pinsNone: No pins to set for this type
swarm.updateConfirm: Update “{name}” over the air: {from} → {to}? The hornet downloads the firmware, restarts and reports the result.
swarm.updateRisk: The ESP-01 keeps the new image beside the old one and cannot roll back: if power fails during the copy, the board must be reflashed over USB. Update one hornet first.
swarm.updateStarted: Update started: progress shows in events
swarm.updateRefused: The update was not started (check the board, the version and the hive address in Settings)
swarm.pinsNotNumber: {field}: '{value}' is not a number. Enter the GPIO number in digits (A0 on the ESP8266 is 17)
swarm.ratioInvalid: Divider ratio: a number above 0 and up to 100, e.g. 5.7

pinHelp.onewire: 1-Wire bus for DS18B20 sensors (meteo role). GPIO number.
pinHelp.onewireEsp8266: NodeMCU and D1 mini default: D5 = GPIO14.
pinHelp.sda: I2C data line for the BME280 and the display (meteo role). GPIO number.
pinHelp.sdaEsp8266: NodeMCU and D1 mini default: D2 = GPIO4.
pinHelp.scl: I2C clock line for the BME280 and the display (meteo role). GPIO number.
pinHelp.sclEsp8266: NodeMCU and D1 mini default: D1 = GPIO5.
pinHelp.relay: Output to the relay module. GPIO number.
pinHelp.relayEsp8266: NodeMCU and D1 mini default: D6 = GPIO12. Numbering: D1=5, D2=4, D5=14, D6=12, D7=13.
pinHelp.button: Local button that toggles the relay, shorts the pin to ground. GPIO number.
pinHelp.buttonEsp8266: NodeMCU default: D3 = GPIO0, the FLASH button on the board.
pinHelp.vbat: Battery or supply voltage through a divider. Works in the meteo and relay roles and arrives as the Battery voltage metric (V), usable in rules. Empty turns it off. Set the divider ratio too.
pinHelp.vbatEsp8266: The ESP8266 has one analog input, A0: enter 17.
pinHelp.vbatEsp32c3: On the ESP32-C3 the ADC is on GPIO0–GPIO4.
pinHelp.ratio:
Voltage divider ratio: (R1 + R2) / R2, R1 being the upper leg (to +), R2 the lower one (to ground). Voltage = pin reading × ratio. Empty = 1.
Example: up to 15 V with R1 = 47 kΩ, R2 = 10 kΩ, ratio 5.7.
+12V → R1 47k → A0 → R2 10k → ground.
Keep the pin at or below 3.2 V (NodeMCU, D1 mini) or 3.3 V (ESP32).
Fine tuning: new ratio = current × (multimeter / hive reading).

swarm.reviveTitle: Bring this hornet back to life on a new board: same name and history

cert.title: Hive certificate (no more browser warning)
cert.hint: The hive serves HTTPS with its own certificate: it has no public name, so the browser warns. Install the hive's root certificate once on each device.

steps.windows: Download the certificate and open the file.|Click "Install Certificate", choose "Local Machine".|Choose "Place all certificates in the following store" → "Trusted Root Certification Authorities".|Restart the browser.
steps.firefox: Open Settings → Privacy & Security → "Certificates" at the bottom → "View Certificates".|"Authorities" tab → "Import" → pick the downloaded file.|Tick "Trust this CA to identify websites" and press OK.|If you added an exception for the hive before, remove it on the "Servers" tab.
steps.android: Download the certificate.|Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate.|Pick the downloaded file and confirm.
steps.iphone: Open this page in Safari and download the certificate, allow the profile download.|Settings → Profile Downloaded → Install.|Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings → turn the hive certificate on.
steps.mac: Download the certificate and open the file: it goes into Keychain Access.|Find it (Caddy Local Authority), open it, Trust → "Always Trust".|Restart the browser.

cert.once: Once per device: the hive certificate is valid for 10 years. It is needed again only if the hive is reinstalled from scratch.

console.title: Hornet console over USB
console.hint: Connect the board to this computer by USB (Chrome or Edge), press Connect and pick the port. This is what the Arduino IDE serial monitor shows, plus ready-made commands. Speed 115200.
console.unsupported: The USB console works only in Chrome and Edge (Firefox has no Web Serial) and on a secure page: open the hive over https://.
console.connected: Connected. If the board sleeps, restart it (the RESET button or Reset below).
console.openFailed: Could not open the port (is another program using it?)
console.resetHint: Restart the board through the RTS line (not every adapter has it wired)
console.empty: What the board writes to its console appears here. Empty? Check the cable and restart the board.
console.rescue: Rescue: bring the board back to the hive network
console.rescueHint: Writes the Wi-Fi saved in the hive Settings (network name and password) into the board and restarts it. If the board has also forgotten the hive address, write that too.
console.rescueConfirm: Write the network "{ssid}" from the hive Settings into the board?
console.rescueDone: Written. Press Restart the board and watch the output.
console.noHiveWifi: No Wi-Fi network and password are saved in the hive Settings
console.setKeys: Settings: set ssid, set pass, set mqtt, set mqttuser, set mqttpass, set id, set upload, set token, set ntp (the value after a space). For a new hornet: enroll <hive address> <code>.
console.factoryConfirm: Erase ALL settings of the board (network, name, keys)? It will have to be set up again.

cmd.show: What the board has stored: name, network, hive address, boot count and the state of a Wi-Fi switch
cmd.awake: Do not sleep until reboot (for battery boards, to have time to set them up)
cmd.factory: Erase all settings of the board
cmd.enroll: join the hive with a one-time code (Wi-Fi must be set); easier with the Enroll button above

console.join: Enroll the board in the hive
console.joinHint: For a new or replaced board whose id and hive address are empty. Choose the hornet it replaces (the code is issued for you); the hive address comes from Settings. The board gets the Wi-Fi from Settings and the enroll command: it fetches its id, broker address, MQTT login and photo token from the hive itself. The hornet record is kept, so history stays.
console.joinNoUrl: The hive address is not set: type it or set it in Settings
console.joinNeedChoice: Choose a hornet or type a code
console.joinConfirm: Write the Wi-Fi '{ssid}' to the board and join the hive {url}? The board will replace the chosen hornet.
console.joinSent: Commands sent, see the board's answer above: 'enrolled ...'
console.brownout: The board restarted because the supply sagged (brownout). Typical for an ESP32-CAM on a weak USB adapter: the current jumps when Wi-Fi starts. Feed 5 V from a proper supply (1 A or more) to the 5V pin and add a 470 uF capacitor between 5V and GND.

tasmota.intro: For a board that already runs Tasmota or OpenBeken (relay, socket, thermostat). The hive gives it a login of its own, limited to its topics, and the lines for its console. How to flash the board itself: docs/tasmota.md.
tasmota.maxOnHint: The relay switches itself off after this time even if the hive is gone. A timed switch-on from the rules is shorter than this.
tasmota.steps: Connect to the board (a Tasmota board shows as tasmota-XXXX, no password) and give it your home network|Open the board's web page, the Console section|Paste the lines one by one, top to bottom, waiting for the answer after each|The board restarts and shows up in the hive as a hornet
tasmota.passwordOnce: The password is shown once and kept nowhere. Lost it: issue the login again, the previous one stops working.
tasmota.waiting: Waiting for the board to reach the hive.
